applies_why: This judge text resolves a collision over Isaiah 7:14 between the sign's chapter-bound verses and C5's narrowed chain, so K-C governs it.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: The phrase 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse' could require express whole-chain weighing or merely forbid resolving by isolated contrary verses; the judge text is read as weighing C5's own narrowed chain/concession against the chapter-bound chain and not as requiring a single stating verse.
why: The judge text does not demand a single verse that states the contrary; it treats the competing chains and word evidence as leaving the link underdetermined, which complies with K-C.
